- If sentiment is positive and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots; model tends to overreact to sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is negative and forecast remains high, force downward correction; model fails to respond to bearish sentiment.
- After a sharp price spike, model often continues upward for 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” rule to reduce forecast slope post-spike.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) and true price drops sharply, model overestimates mean reversion; adjust forecast to reflect more aggressive downward drift.
- If history shows recent mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline), model tends to ignore it; apply a “reversion bias” correction to forecast downward trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome drops below 80% of 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in continuation.
- If sentiment history shows multiple 0.00 entries, model often overestimates volatility; apply a “sentiment dampening” rule to smooth forecast curve.
